landingAreas.name: Aire de poser principale - pelouse tondue autour de la cible
landingAreas.evidence: Traced on Esri z18 and IGN z18/z19: the bright, regularly mown grass bowl (~1.30 ha) between the curving gravel path (west) and the vegetated overflow channel (east). It is where the club's circuit diagram puts the finals, the windsock and the aim point; IGN shows a canopy on the ground and people here. The club does not publish separate student/tandem areas: everyone lands here.

landingAreas.name: Reste de la zone d'atterrissage du club (bande ouest de la piste + bras de décharge)
landingAreas.evidence: The orange 'ZONE D'ATTERRISSAGE' outline on the club diagrams (circuit-sous-voile-chambery.jpg, vertical-terrain.jpg): the ~70-150 m wide strip west of the airport perimeter track, from about 45.6383 N down to the curve at the south end (~8.3 ha, excludes the bowl). Its middle is the 'Bras de décharge de la Leysse' (OSM way 169787103, intermittent overflow channel), a sinuous swale with taller, darker vegetation (#2d4b2a on Esri), flanked by dry rough grass (#706c52). North end latitude estimated from the club photos (+-50 m).

target.surface: grass with a small white marker
target.evidence: A small white object (~1-2 m) at the same spot on Esri z18/z19 (45.630366,5.877460) and on IGN z19 (canopy and people at 45.630401,5.877412), and a white dot at that place in the club's 2021-22 oblique photo. pattern.description: Pattern always flown WEST of the landing area, over the fields between the landing strip and the D1504 road, never over the runway. Club diagram: rendezvous point ('point de RDV') at 250 m AGL on the west side, around 45.6320 N 5.8750 E (over the hedge/tree row east of the D1504). Landing towards the lake (north wind, crosswind or no wind): 'circuit Nord, main gauche' = left-hand: downwind southbound along ~5.8750 E, left base eastbound along ~45.6289 N, final northbound on ~5.8774 E to the target. South wind: 'circuit Sud, main droite' = right-hand: downwind northbound along ~5.8750 E, right base eastbound along ~45.6342 N, final southbound to the target. Rectangle corners from the club diagram, +-50 m: NW 45.6342,5.8750 / NE 45.6342,5.8775 / SE 45.6289,5.8775 / SW 45.6289,5.8750.
pattern.noOverfly: No runway crossing below 600 m (the red 'zone aéroport' = runway, taxiways, aprons, terminal): if open over the runway or east of it, come back west; if too low to cross, land in the fields east of the airport. Avoid: the Savoie Technolac / university campus buildings NW (45.636-45.645 N, 5.868-5.876 E), the houses of Le Tremblay/Villarcher SW and the retail/industrial zone 'La Prairie' S of the field (45.624-45.628 N), the D1504 road and the 20 kV overhead line just west of it (Enedis, OSM way 516666063: 45.6307,5.8720 -> 45.6252,5.8729), the wooded Leysse banks further west, and the Lac du Bourget 2.3 km north (water landing).
pattern.landingDirection: 'Posé face au lac' (land heading north, towards the lake) with north wind, crosswind or no wind; land heading south only with a south wind. Prevailing summer afternoon wind is from the north (lake breeze), so northbound finals are the norm.
pattern.holdingArea: 'Zone d'évolution Nord' (blue on the club map: west of the landing strip, from the RDV latitude 45.632 N up to the Technolac, ~5.869-5.876 E) and 'Zone d'évolution Sud' (yellow: south-west, ~45.623-45.632 N, 5.868-5.875 E, fields and the Leysse woods); stack there, then join the RDV point at 250 m.

jumpRun.aircraft: Pilatus PC-6/B2-H4 Turbo Porter F-GIBV 'Bravo Victor' (white with magenta/black trim), 10 jumpers + pilot, ~15 min to 4000 m, exit at ~140 km/h
jumpRun.description: Exit 4000 m above the ground ('au-dessus du lac'), PJE 417 SFC-FL140, centre 45.6336 N 5.8775 E. Tandem opening ~1500 m; minimum openings 1000/850 m by licence. Jump-run line not published: assumed along the valley axis (N-S), into wind, so with the usual north wind the run is flown northbound along the runway and exits are roughly 1-2 km north of the landing area, between the north half of the airfield and the south shore of the lake; with a south wind, southbound with exits over the plain south of the field. Tandems leave one by one with intervals. Guessed, not documented.

wind.station: LFLB METAR (Chambéry Aix-les-Bains, Météo-France anemometer on the airfield at 45.6415 N 5.8780 E, 1.3 km N of the landing area), via Iowa Environmental Mesonet
wind.period: 2015-01-01 to 2024-12-31, June-September, 07:00-17:00 UTC = 09:00-19:00 local (CEST); 25344 half-hourly reports
wind.notes: Shares are of reports with a direction (they sum to 1); in addition 2.4% calm and 21.9% variable (VRB, light, mostly mornings). Median speed of all daytime reports 9.3 km/h; north-quadrant (315-045) median 11.1 km/h, vector-mean direction 357°; 90th percentile 17 km/h; >25 km/h only 1.2% of reports. Strong thermal pattern along the N-S valley axis: at night and until ~09:00 a weak down-valley wind from the S (Chambéry side, ~4 km/h); from 10-11 h the lake breeze / up-valley wind sets in from the N (lake side), 55% of reports at 11 h, 75-80% at 13-16 h, ~11 km/h, fading after 19 h. South-sector winds (160-200°) are the synoptic / föhn-type days, 8% of daytime reports, ~11-13 km/h. E-W components are rare (<5%) because the Mont du Chat ridge (W) and the Revard-Nivolet escarpment (E) channel the flow. LFLE (Challes-les-Eaux) has no METAR. Default: 'usual' = from 360° (north) 10 km/h at 10 m; 360 rather than 0 so it can't be mistaken for calm.

colors.notes: Suggested albedo-like colours, brightened from imagery samples (Esri is contrasty and dark in greens, Sentinel-2 cloudless is raw and very dark, IGN is hazy). Raw samples: airfield grass Esri #777050 W of runway, #827157 E (mown/hayed, straw), IGN #968d7a; landing bowl Esri #375c2f, IGN #6c7465 (mown, stays green); overflow-channel swale Esri #2d4b2a; dry rough grass of the strip #706c52; fields: harvested cereal Esri #a68468, green crops #2b5228/#123123, mixed #6b7355; forest Mont du Chat Esri #2c4d32 / S2 #122310; alpine pasture S2 Margériaz #555e3f; Granier cliff/scar S2 #737b72 (pale Urgonian limestone, cream-grey in sun); Lac du Bourget Esri #054f4e (deep teal), lake rim shallow turquoise ~#3f8f86 visible in Esri; runway asphalt Esri #6b716d (IGN #bbb7af, light grey). Fields palette = stubble, ripe wheat (guessed), maize/soy, hay meadow, bare soil. The airfield grass is mown and partly cut for hay: in June it is green (#5d7a3c), from July it is mostly straw-coloured.

landmarks.name: Lac du Bourget (south shore at the airfield)
landmarks.why: Water level ~231.5 m. The shore is 2.3 km N of the landing area, ~380 m beyond the runway 18 threshold; landing pattern 'face au lac'. The lake runs 18 km to the NNW.

landmarks.name: Lac du Bourget (centre)
landmarks.why: Largest natural lake in France, 18 x 3 km, deep teal; dominates the view to the N from canopy and from 4000 m.

landmarks.name: Dent du Chat
landmarks.why: Rock tooth on the ridge above the W shore of the lake, 6 km NW; the classic skyline W of the DZ.

landmarks.name: Signal du Mont du Chat (TV mast)
landmarks.why: Highest point of the ridge to the WNW (5.5 km), with a large relay mast; the ridge (1400-1500 m) closes the valley on the W side.

landmarks.name: Col du Chat
landmarks.why: Road pass/tunnel over the Mont du Chat ridge, 7 km NNW.

landmarks.name: Mont Revard
landmarks.why: Edge of the Bauges plateau with cliffs above Aix-les-Bains, 9.5 km NE.

landmarks.name: Croix du Nivolet (Dent du Nivolet)
landmarks.why: Big illuminated cross on the cliff edge above Chambéry, 7 km ESE; seen from everywhere in the valley.

landmarks.name: Mont Margériaz
landmarks.why: Bauges summit with ski area / alpine pastures, 12 km E.

landmarks.name: Mont Trélod
landmarks.why: Bauges, 25 km ENE.

landmarks.name: Pointe d'Arcalod

landmarks.name: Mont Colombier (Bauges)
landmarks.why: Bauges, 19 km E.

landmarks.name: Mont Granier
landmarks.why: Huge pale limestone N face (1248 landslide scar) closing the Chambéry valley to the S, 19 km SSE; northern bastion of the Chartreuse.

landmarks.name: Mont Outheran
landmarks.why: Chartreuse, 19 km S.

landmarks.name: Dent de Crolles
landmarks.why: Chartreuse cliff, 36 km S, visible from altitude.

landmarks.name: Chamechaude
landmarks.why: Highest summit of the Chartreuse, 39 km S.

landmarks.name: Grand Colon
landmarks.why: Belledonne, 52 km S.

landmarks.name: Grand Pic de Belledonne
landmarks.why: Belledonne range, 52 km SSE, often snowy until early summer; seen from 4000 m.

landmarks.name: Mont Blanc
landmarks.why: 79 km ENE; the club says it is visible from 4000 m on clear days.

landmarks.name: Mont Saint-Michel (Savoie)
landmarks.why: Wooded hill above Challes-les-Eaux and the LFLE glider field, 13 km SE; not near this DZ.

landmarks.name: Chambéry (Château des Ducs de Savoie)
landmarks.why: Old town and castle, 8 km SSE; the town fills the valley floor S of the field.

landmarks.name: Aix-les-Bains
landmarks.why: Spa town on the E shore, 7 km NNE.

landmarks.name: Savoie Technolac / university campus (Le Bourget-du-Lac)
landmarks.why: Office blocks and campus immediately NNW of the landing strip (0.5-1.5 km): no-overfly at low height.

landmarks.name: Abbaye d'Hautecombe
landmarks.why: Abbey on the W shore of the lake, 14 km NNW.

landmarks.name: Lac d'Aiguebelette
landmarks.why: Small turquoise lake behind the Épine ridge, 10 km SW; named by the club as visible from 4000 m.

landmarks.name: Lac d'Annecy
landmarks.why: 33 km NE, visible from altitude.

landmarks.name: A41 motorway (Chambéry-Annecy)
landmarks.why: Passes 3.1 km ENE of the landing area, behind the Voglans hill.

landmarks.name: A43 motorway (to Lyon, via Tunnel de l'Épine)
landmarks.why: 3 km S of the field, curving W towards the Épine tunnel.

landmarks.name: A41 / A43 / N201 (VRU) junction
landmarks.why: Motorway junction at the N edge of Chambéry, 3.1 km SSE.

landmarks.name: D1201 (VRU Chambéry)
landmarks.why: Dual carriageway along the E edge of the airfield, ~1.1 km E of the landing area.

invented: Second DZ windsock (45.62945, 5.87635): placed from the club's 2021-22 oblique photo only, not visible on imagery (+-20 m).
North end of the club's landing strip (45.6383 N): estimated from the club photos (+-50 m); south part and bowl are traced on imagery.
Pattern rectangle corners and the RDV point (45.6320, 5.8750, 250 m): read off the club's schematic circuit diagram, +-50 m.
Jump run: direction (N-S along the valley, into wind) and exit point (over the south shore of the lake with N wind) are inferred, not published.

Building heights: SP main building and Rectimo from IGN shadows (+-1.5 m); chalet and other hangars guessed. Wall colours guessed except SP grey cladding and chalet timber (club photos). hangarDoor flags guessed.
Target: only a small white marker shows; its exact form (disc, cross) and the 1.5 m radius are guesses.
Taxiway polygons are OSM centrelines buffered to widths measured approximately on imagery (S 11 m, N/N1/N2/C 15 m); runway-18 turn pad traced at z17 (+-3 m).
Holding areas ('zones d'évolution') extents are approximate from the club diagram.
Colour hexes are brightened interpretations of imagery samples, not measured albedo.
Aircraft livery colours from one club photo (white, magenta, black).
